name: Rafu
title: Father of Palti from the tribe of Benjamin
summary: Rafu was the father of Palti, who served as the representative from the tribe of Benjamin among the twelve spies that Moses sent into the land of Canaan. Rafu is mentioned only in connection with his son Palti's mission, and his role is limited to being identified as a father in the tribe's genealogy.

keyEvents.title: The Appointment of the Spies
keyEvents.description: Moses sent twelve men to spy out the land of Canaan, one from each tribe. Palti, son of Rafu, was chosen to represent the tribe of Benjamin.

keyEvents.title: The Spies' Mission in Canaan
keyEvents.description: The twelve spies, including Palti's son Rafu, were sent out to explore the land, its people, cities, and fertility over a period of forty days.

keyEvents.title: The Spies Return with a Negative Report
keyEvents.description: Ten of the twelve spies, likely including Palti son of Rafu, returned with a negative report stating that the land could not be conquered, which led to the people's rebellion.

keyEvents.title: The People's Rebellion and God's Judgment
keyEvents.description: As a result of the spies' negative report and the people's rebellion, God judged the generation wandering in the wilderness to die there without reaching the promised land.
